cards.front: What are the key features of glioblastoma?
cards.back: The most common **malignant primary** brain tumor in adults. It grows in the cerebral hemispheres and can cross the **corpus callosum** (*butterfly glioma*). Histology: **pseudopalisading** tumor cells around **necrosis**, plus vascular proliferation. **GFAP**-positive. Very poor prognosis.
cards.back_pt: O tumor cerebral **primário maligno** mais comum em adultos. Cresce nos hemisférios cerebrais e pode atravessar o **corpo caloso** (*butterfly glioma*, glioma em asa de borboleta). Histologia: células tumorais em **pseudopaliçada** ao redor de **necrose**, além de proliferação vascular. **GFAP** positivo. Prognóstico muito ruim.

cards.front: What are the typical features of a meningioma?
cards.back: The most common **benign** primary brain tumor; more common in **women**. It comes from **arachnoid cap cells**, so it is **extra-axial** and attached to the **dura**. Histology: **whorls** of cells and **psammoma bodies**. Linked to **NF2** and prior radiation.
cards.back_pt: O tumor cerebral primário **benigno** mais comum; mais frequente em **mulheres**. Origina-se de **células da capa aracnoide**, por isso é **extra-axial** e aderido à **dura-máter**. Histologia: **redemoinhos** (*whorls*) de células e **corpos psamomatosos**. Associado a **NF2** e a radioterapia prévia.

cards.front: A tumor at the cerebellopontine angle causes one-sided hearing loss and tinnitus. What is it?
cards.back: **Vestibular schwannoma**: a tumor of the Schwann cells of **CN VIII**, often growing in the **internal auditory canal**. The cells are **S-100**-positive (neural crest origin). **Bilateral** tumors suggest **NF2**.
cards.back_pt: **Schwannoma vestibular**: tumor das células de Schwann do **NC VIII**, que muitas vezes cresce no **meato acústico interno**. As células são **S-100** positivas (origem na crista neural). Tumores **bilaterais** sugerem **NF2**.

cards.front: Which adult glioma shows 'fried egg' cells and calcifications?
cards.back: **Oligodendroglioma**: usually in the **frontal lobe**, often presenting with **seizures**. Round nuclei with clear cytoplasm (*fried egg*), branching *chicken-wire* capillaries and frequent **calcifications**. Defined by an **IDH mutation** plus **1p/19q codeletion**.
cards.back_pt: **Oligodendroglioma**: geralmente no **lobo frontal**, muitas vezes com **crises epilépticas**. Núcleos redondos com citoplasma claro (*fried egg*, ovo frito), capilares ramificados em *chicken-wire* (tela de galinheiro) e **calcificações** frequentes. Definido por **mutação de IDH** e **codeleção 1p/19q**.

cards.front: A child has a midline cerebellar tumor with Homer-Wright rosettes. What is it, and how does it spread?
cards.back: **Medulloblastoma**: a malignant **embryonal** tumor of the **cerebellar vermis** made of small round blue cells. It can block the **fourth ventricle** (hydrocephalus). It spreads through the CSF and causes **drop metastases** to the spinal cord.
cards.back_pt: **Meduloblastoma**: tumor **embrionário** maligno do **vérmis cerebelar**, formado por pequenas células redondas e azuis. Pode obstruir o **quarto ventrículo** (hidrocefalia). Dissemina-se pelo LCR e causa **metástases em gota** (*drop metastases*) para a medula espinal.

cards.front: Which bacteria most often cause meningitis at each age?
cards.back: **Neonates**: **group B streptococcus**, **E. coli**, **Listeria**. **Children and adults**: **Streptococcus pneumoniae** and **Neisseria meningitidis** (often adolescents and young adults). **Older adults**: mainly *S. pneumoniae*; add **Listeria** (also in immunosuppression). **Haemophilus influenzae type b** is now rare after vaccination.
cards.back_pt: **Recém-nascidos**: **estreptococo do grupo B**, **E. coli**, **Listeria**. **Crianças e adultos**: **Streptococcus pneumoniae** e **Neisseria meningitidis** (muitas vezes adolescentes e adultos jovens). **Idosos**: principalmente *S. pneumoniae*; acrescente **Listeria** (também na imunossupressão). O **Haemophilus influenzae tipo b** hoje é raro graças à vacinação.

cards.front: How does the CSF differ in bacterial, viral, and tuberculous or fungal meningitis?
cards.back: **Bacterial**: **neutrophils**, **low glucose**, high protein. **Viral**: **lymphocytes**, **normal glucose**, normal or mildly high protein. **TB or fungal**: **lymphocytes**, **low glucose**, high protein. Opening pressure is high in bacterial, TB and fungal disease.
cards.back_pt: **Bacteriana**: **neutrófilos**, **glicose baixa**, proteína alta. **Viral**: **linfócitos**, **glicose normal**, proteína normal ou pouco elevada. **Tuberculosa ou fúngica**: **linfócitos**, **glicose baixa**, proteína alta. A pressão de abertura é alta na bacteriana, na tuberculosa e na fúngica.

cards.front: What does each brain herniation syndrome compress?
cards.back: **Subfalcine** (cingulate gyrus under the falx): **ACA**, so contralateral leg weakness. **Uncal**: ipsilateral **CN III** (dilated pupil, then a *down and out* eye) and the **PCA**. **Tonsillar** (through the foramen magnum): the **medulla**, causing respiratory and cardiac arrest.
cards.back_pt: **Subfalcina** (giro do cíngulo sob a foice): **ACA**, com fraqueza da perna contralateral. **Uncal**: **NC III** ipsilateral (pupila dilatada, depois olho *down and out*, para baixo e para fora) e a **ACP**. **Tonsilar** (pelo forame magno): o **bulbo**, causando parada respiratória e cardíaca.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy has had morning headaches and vomiting for 2 months. His parents say he has become clumsy. Exam shows papilledema, a wide-based gait and dysmetria of the left arm. MRI shows a well-defined cystic mass in the left cerebellar hemisphere with a contrast-enhancing nodule in its wall. The tumor is removed. Microscopy shows elongated cells with thin, hair-like processes and bright eosinophilic, corkscrew-shaped fibers. Which tumor is this?
questions.explanation: A cerebellar **cyst with a mural nodule** in a child, with hair-like (*piloid*) cells and **Rosenthal fibers** (eosinophilic corkscrew fibers), is a **pilocytic astrocytoma**, a low-grade tumor with a good prognosis. **Hemangioblastoma** can also look like a cerebellar cyst with a nodule, but it usually occurs in adults (often with **VHL**) and shows foamy stromal cells between many capillaries, not Rosenthal fibers. Medulloblastoma is a solid midline vermis tumor of small round blue cells.
questions.explanation_pt: Um **cisto com nódulo mural** no cerebelo de uma criança, com células pilosas (*piloid*) e **fibras de Rosenthal** (fibras eosinofílicas em saca-rolhas), é um **astrocitoma pilocítico**, tumor de baixo grau com bom prognóstico. O **hemangioblastoma** também pode aparecer como cisto cerebelar com nódulo, mas costuma ocorrer em adultos (muitas vezes com **VHL**) e mostra células estromais espumosas entre muitos capilares, e não fibras de Rosenthal. O meduloblastoma é um tumor sólido da linha média (vérmis), de pequenas células redondas e azuis.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man who recently moved from a region where tuberculosis is common has had headache, low-grade fever, night sweats and weight loss for 3 weeks. In the last 2 days he has become confused and sees double. Exam shows neck stiffness, and he cannot abduct his right eye. Lumbar puncture shows a high opening pressure. CSF: 250 white cells/µL with 85% lymphocytes, glucose 25 mg/dL (serum glucose 100 mg/dL) and protein 220 mg/dL. Gram stain shows no organisms. MRI shows enhancement of the meninges at the base of the brain. Which organism is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: A **subacute** course over weeks, **basilar meningeal enhancement** and a **cranial nerve palsy** (here CN VI), with CSF showing **lymphocytes**, **low glucose** and very **high protein**, point to **tuberculous meningitis**. Enteroviruses also cause a lymphocytic CSF, but glucose stays normal and the illness is acute and usually mild. *S. pneumoniae* and *N. meningitidis* also lower glucose, but they cause an acute illness with a **neutrophilic** CSF.
questions.explanation_pt: Um curso **subagudo** ao longo de semanas, **realce meníngeo basal** e **paralisia de nervo craniano** (aqui o NC VI), com LCR mostrando **linfócitos**, **glicose baixa** e **proteína muito alta**, indicam **meningite tuberculosa**. Os enterovírus também causam LCR linfocítico, mas a glicose fica normal e o quadro é agudo e geralmente leve. *S. pneumoniae* e *N. meningitidis* também reduzem a glicose, mas causam quadro agudo com LCR **neutrofílico**.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman has had fever and headache for 3 days. Today her husband says she is acting strangely and has trouble finding words. She reports smelling burning rubber, and she has a focal seizure in the emergency department. Temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F). MRI shows T2 hyperintensity and swelling in the left medial temporal lobe. CSF shows a lymphocytic pleocytosis, many red blood cells, normal glucose and mildly high protein. Which organism is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Fever, behavior change, aphasia, **olfactory hallucinations** and seizures with **temporal lobe** involvement and red cells in the CSF point to **HSV-1 encephalitis**, the most common cause of sporadic viral encephalitis in adults. It causes **hemorrhagic necrosis**, and infected cells show **Cowdry A** intranuclear inclusions. **HSV-2** is the tempting choice, but in adults it usually causes (sometimes recurrent) **meningitis**, not encephalitis; HSV-2 encephalitis is mainly a **neonatal** infection acquired during birth. JC virus causes PML in immunocompromised patients, without fever.
questions.explanation_pt: Febre, alteração de comportamento, afasia, **alucinações olfatórias** e crises epilépticas com acometimento do **lobo temporal** e hemácias no LCR indicam **encefalite por HSV-1**, a causa mais comum de encefalite viral esporádica em adultos. Ela causa **necrose hemorrágica**, e as células infectadas mostram inclusões intranucleares **Cowdry A**. O **HSV-2** é a escolha tentadora, mas em adultos geralmente causa **meningite** (às vezes recorrente), e não encefalite; a encefalite por HSV-2 é principalmente uma infecção **neonatal**, adquirida no parto. O vírus JC causa LEMP em imunossuprimidos, sem febre.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man with a known glioblastoma in the left temporal lobe is found by his wife to be very drowsy, and within an hour he stops responding. Blood pressure is 182/90 mm Hg, pulse is 48/min, and his breathing is irregular. The left pupil is dilated and does not react to light, and the left eye rests down and out. CT shows a large left temporal mass with surrounding edema and shift of the midline to the right. Compression of which structure best explains his left eye findings?
choices: Dorsal midbrain at the superior colliculi
questions.explanation: A growing mass pushes the medial temporal lobe (**uncus**) over the tentorium, compressing the ipsilateral **oculomotor nerve**. Its outer **parasympathetic** fibers are hit first, so the pupil dilates; later the eye turns **down and out** because CN IV and CN VI are unopposed. The **posterior cerebral artery** is also compressed in uncal herniation, but that causes occipital infarction, not these eye findings. High blood pressure, bradycardia and irregular breathing form the **Cushing triad** of raised intracranial pressure.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma massa em expansão empurra a parte medial do lobo temporal (**unco**) sobre o tentório, comprimindo o **nervo oculomotor** ipsilateral. Suas fibras **parassimpáticas** externas são afetadas primeiro, então a pupila se dilata; depois o olho fica **para baixo e para fora**, porque o NC IV e o NC VI agem sem oposição. A **artéria cerebral posterior** também é comprimida na herniação uncal, mas isso causa infarto occipital, e não esses achados oculares. Hipertensão, bradicardia e respiração irregular formam a **tríade de Cushing** da hipertensão intracraniana.

notes.title: CNS tumors, infections and trauma
notes.body_md:
## Primary tumors in adults

- **Glioblastoma**: most common **malignant** primary; crosses the corpus callosum (*butterfly*); **pseudopalisading necrosis**; **GFAP**-positive.
- **Meningioma**: most common benign; dural-based and extra-axial; **psammoma bodies**; women, **NF2**.
- **Vestibular schwannoma**: CN VIII in the internal auditory canal; **S-100**-positive; bilateral in **NF2**.
- **Oligodendroglioma**: frontal lobe, seizures, calcifications, *fried egg* cells, **1p/19q codeletion**.
- **Hemangioblastoma**: cerebellum; linked to **VHL** (see the endocrine neoplasia block).
- **Primary CNS lymphoma**: B-cell; in **AIDS** it is linked to **EBV**.

## Primary tumors in children

- Many arise in the **posterior fossa**.
- **Pilocytic astrocytoma**: cerebellar cyst with a mural nodule, **Rosenthal fibers**, good prognosis.
- **Medulloblastoma**: vermis, **Homer-Wright rosettes**, **drop metastases**.
- **Ependymoma**: **fourth ventricle**, perivascular pseudorosettes, **hydrocephalus**.
- **Craniopharyngioma**: suprasellar, from Rathke pouch remnants (see the pituitary block).

## Metastases

- The **most common** brain tumors overall; often **multiple**, at the **gray-white junction**.
- Common sources: **lung**, **breast**, **melanoma**, **kidney**, **colon**.

## Infections

- **Bacterial meningitis**: CSF neutrophils and low glucose; organisms vary by age.
- **HSV-1 encephalitis**: **temporal lobe**, hemorrhagic necrosis, **Cowdry A** inclusions.
- **Ring-enhancing lesions in AIDS**: **toxoplasmosis** (usually multiple) or **lymphoma** (often single).
- **Brain abscess**: often streptococci or *S. aureus*, from sinus or dental infection or blood spread.
- **Neurocysticercosis**: ingested *Taenia solium* eggs form brain cysts that cause **seizures**.
- **Rabies**: **Negri bodies** in neurons.

## Trauma, herniation and pressure

- **Contusion**: **coup** (impact side) and **contrecoup** (opposite side); frontal and temporal poles.
- **Diffuse axonal injury**: rotational shearing; coma with a near-normal first CT.
- **Uncal herniation**: ipsilateral **CN III** palsy (dilated pupil first) and **PCA** compression.
- **Subfalcine**: **ACA** compression. **Tonsillar**: medulla compression, cardiorespiratory arrest.
- Downward **transtentorial** (uncal or central) herniation stretches and tears paramedian basilar artery branches in the midbrain and pons: **Duret hemorrhages**, usually fatal.
- **Cushing triad** of raised intracranial pressure: **hypertension**, **bradycardia**, **irregular breathing**.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Tumores primários em adultos

- **Glioblastoma**: o primário **maligno** mais comum; atravessa o corpo caloso (*butterfly*, em asa de borboleta); **necrose em pseudopaliçada**; **GFAP** positivo.
- **Meningioma**: o benigno mais comum; aderido à dura-máter e extra-axial; **corpos psamomatosos**; mulheres, **NF2**.
- **Schwannoma vestibular**: NC VIII no meato acústico interno; **S-100** positivo; bilateral na **NF2**.
- **Oligodendroglioma**: lobo frontal, crises epilépticas, calcificações, células em *fried egg* (ovo frito), **codeleção 1p/19q**.
- **Hemangioblastoma**: cerebelo; associado a **VHL** (ver o bloco de neoplasias endócrinas).
- **Linfoma primário do SNC**: de células B; na **AIDS** está associado ao **EBV**.

## Tumores primários em crianças

- Muitos surgem na **fossa posterior**.
- **Astrocitoma pilocítico**: cisto cerebelar com nódulo mural, **fibras de Rosenthal**, bom prognóstico.
- **Meduloblastoma**: vérmis, **rosetas de Homer-Wright**, **metástases em gota**.
- **Ependimoma**: **quarto ventrículo**, pseudorrosetas perivasculares, **hidrocefalia**.
- **Craniofaringioma**: suprasselar, a partir de restos da bolsa de Rathke (ver o bloco de hipófise).

## Metástases

- São os tumores cerebrais **mais comuns** no geral; muitas vezes **múltiplas**, na **junção entre substância cinzenta e branca**.
- Origens comuns: **pulmão**, **mama**, **melanoma**, **rim**, **cólon**.

## Infecções

- **Meningite bacteriana**: neutrófilos e glicose baixa no LCR; os agentes variam com a idade.
- **Encefalite por HSV-1**: **lobo temporal**, necrose hemorrágica, inclusões **Cowdry A**.
- **Lesões com realce em anel na AIDS**: **toxoplasmose** (geralmente múltiplas) ou **linfoma** (muitas vezes única).
- **Abscesso cerebral**: muitas vezes estreptococos ou *S. aureus*, a partir de infecção sinusal ou odontológica ou por via hematogênica.
- **Neurocisticercose**: ovos de *Taenia solium* ingeridos formam cistos cerebrais que causam **crises epilépticas**.
- **Raiva**: **corpúsculos de Negri** nos neurônios.

## Trauma, herniação e pressão

- **Contusão**: **golpe** (lado do impacto) e **contragolpe** (lado oposto); polos frontais e temporais.
- **Lesão axonal difusa**: cisalhamento rotacional; coma com primeira TC quase normal.
- **Herniação uncal**: paralisia do **NC III** ipsilateral (pupila dilatada primeiro) e compressão da **ACP**.
- **Subfalcina**: compressão da **ACA**. **Tonsilar**: compressão do bulbo, parada cardiorrespiratória.
- A herniação **transtentorial** descendente (uncal ou central) estira e rompe ramos paramedianos da artéria basilar no mesencéfalo e na ponte: **hemorragias de Duret**, geralmente fatais.
- **Tríade de Cushing** da hipertensão intracraniana: **hipertensão arterial**, **bradicardia**, **respiração irregular**.
